# SK8021 — The test class declares no test

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A class marked `[TestClass]` or `[TestFixture]` declares no test method, in itself or in any base type, so the runner opens it and reports nothing about it.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Tests |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 1.3 |
| Supersedes | S2187 |

## Why

The attribute is a declaration of intent that the file no longer keeps. A fixture that lost its last test to a refactor — renamed away, moved to another class, commented out during a bisect and never restored — still looks exactly like a fixture that passes, because a class with nothing to run produces no output of any kind. It is `SK8020`'s silence approached from the other side, and like `SK8020` it is decided from attributes alone: the question is whether any method on the type or on a base type carries a test attribute, and answering it follows no call. That is what keeps it out of the territory `SK8001` was cut for.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
[TestClass]
public sealed class ArchetypeTests {
    static Archetype Build() => new();
}
```

Write:

```csharp
[TestClass]
public sealed class ArchetypeTests {
    static Archetype Build() => new();

    [TestMethod]
    public void Counts() {
        Assert.AreEqual(0, Build().Count);
    }
}
```

## When it does not fire

⚠ **MSTest and NUnit only, and xUnit's absence is a decision.** xUnit has no class-level attribute, so there is no declaration of intent for an empty class to contradict; covering it would mean deciding from the class's *name* that it was meant to hold tests, which is a convention rather than a fact and is the guess this rule exists not to make. ⚠ **Inherited tests are tests.** The search walks the whole base chain, including base types that live in another assembly, so the common shared-fixture shape — an annotated base holding the cases and a derived class parameterising them — is silence. ⚠ **A lifecycle hook makes the attribute meaningful and stops the rule.** MSTest requires `[TestClass]` on the type holding `[AssemblyInitialize]` or `[AssemblyCleanup]`, so a hooks-only class is correct code that this rule must not report; `[ClassInitialize]`, `[ClassCleanup]`, `[TestInitialize]`, `[TestCleanup]` and NUnit's `[SetUp]`, `[TearDown]`, `[OneTimeSetUp]` and `[OneTimeTearDown]` are treated the same way. ⚠ **`abstract` never fires**, which is the escape hatch for the shared-base pattern and also for the residual case this rule does not decide: a *concrete* annotated base class that exists only for its derived fixtures to extend will be reported, and marking it `abstract` — which it almost always should be — is both the suppression and the repair. ⚠ **One finding per type, not per partial part.** ⚠ **`hasFix: false`, and there is no version of this that has one.** The two repairs are to write the test the file is missing and to delete the class, and choosing between them is the entire content of the finding; an edit that picked one would be the tool deciding whether a piece of test coverage was meant to exist.

## Configuration

- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK8021.severity`
